old: The effective overburden divided by the frictional ratio, plus the pore pressure and the unconfined compressive strength.
new: The effective overburden over the frictional ratio, plus the pore pressure and the compressive strength.

old: At forty-five degrees from the high side, where the shear stress at the wall of the hole reaches its maximum value.
new: At forty-five degrees from the high side, where the shear stress at the wall is at its maximum.

old: More golden files at more conditions.
new: More golden files at more conditions, so the oracle agreement covers every attitude and depth.

old: Fully validated against North Sea field data.
new: Fully validated against North Sea field data, since the Horsrud correlation was fitted on North Sea shales.

old: An average of several offset wells in the same field, resampled onto a common depth grid at fifty metre intervals.
new: An average of offset wells in the same field, resampled onto a common fifty metre grid.

old: Which engine, which version, which author.
new: Which engine, which version, which author, since those decide how far the output can be trusted.

old: The rock has no strength there, so any mud weight at all will cause the wall to fail immediately upon exposure.
new: The rock has no strength there, so any mud weight will make the wall fail on exposure.

old: The search range was set too low and the calculation should be repeated with a wider bracket around the expected value.
new: The search range was too low; repeat with a wider bracket.

old: The collapse and fracture pressures coincide, which is the definition of a marginally stable wellbore.
new: The collapse and fracture pressures coincide: a marginally stable hole.

old: A stress larger than the overburden.
new: A stress larger than the overburden anywhere in the section, flagged by the quality score.

old: A blank cell, since the engine returns a null rather than a number when the criterion is satisfied at zero pressure.
new: A blank cell, since the engine returns a null when the criterion is satisfied at zero pressure.

old: Stops the walk at that depth.
new: Stops the walk at that depth, since nothing deeper in the hole can then be trusted.

old: Because a report must present them in a standard order for the results to be comparable between wells.
new: Because a report must present them in a standard order to be comparable between wells.

old: The full theta sweep at the tightest depth, so that the breakout width can be estimated from the margin profile.
new: The full theta sweep at the tightest depth, so breakout width can be read from the margins.

old: The tightest point on each well, which the Expert tier then uses to design the mud programme per section.
new: The tightest point on each well, which the Expert tier uses to design the mud programme.

old: Use a coarser theta grid, since the hoop stress pattern on a vertical hole is smooth and needs fewer sample points.
new: Use a coarser theta grid, since the hoop stress on a vertical hole is smooth and needs few points.

old: Always use the pore pressure.
new: Always use the pore pressure, because a kick is the more immediate hazard on any drilling well.

old: Round it up to the nearest fifty kilograms per cubic metre, which is the resolution at which mud weight is actually controlled.
new: Round it up to the nearest fifty kilograms per cubic metre, as mud is controlled.

old: Compare it against the pore pressure and report only the larger, since that is the number the driller acts on.
new: Compare it with the pore pressure and report only the larger, the number drilled to.

old: The breakout angle changes, since the stress ratio at the wall depends on the depth through the effective stresses.
new: The breakout angle shifts, since the wall stress ratio varies with depth.

old: What the breakout angle will be.
new: What the breakout angle will be, since that is the output most easily checked on an image log.
